draft.title: Graphs of sine and cosine
card: The graph of \(y = \sin x\) starts at 0 when \(x = 0^{\circ}\). It rises to 1 at \(90^{\circ}\), falls to 0 at \(180^{\circ}\), reaches \(-1\) at \(270^{\circ}\), and is back at 0 at \(360^{\circ}\).
The graph of \(y = \cos x\) starts at 1 when \(x = 0^{\circ}\). It falls to 0 at \(90^{\circ}\), reaches \(-1\) at \(180^{\circ}\), is back at 0 at \(270^{\circ}\), and ends at 1 at \(360^{\circ}\).
Both graphs are smooth waves with the same shape. Their highest value is 1 and their lowest value is \(-1\). They differ in where they start.

1.alt: The graph of \(y = \sin x\) from \(0^{\circ}\) to \(360^{\circ}\). It crosses the x-axis at \(0^{\circ}\), \(180^{\circ}\) and \(360^{\circ}\), has its highest point \((90, 1)\) and its lowest point \((270, -1)\).

2.alt: The graph of \(y = \cos x\) from \(0^{\circ}\) to \(360^{\circ}\). It starts at \((0, 1)\), crosses the x-axis at \(90^{\circ}\) and \(270^{\circ}\), has its lowest point \((180, -1)\) and ends at \((360, 1)\).

draft.remember: Both waves stay between \(-1\) and \(1\). Sine starts at 0, and cosine starts at 1.

a.q: Which statement is true for the graph of \(y = \sin x\) from \(0^{\circ}\) to \(360^{\circ}\)?
opts: It crosses the x-axis at \(0^{\circ}\), \(180^{\circ}\) and \(360^{\circ}\)
It crosses the x-axis at \(90^{\circ}\) and \(270^{\circ}\)
It starts at 1 and falls to \(-1\) at \(180^{\circ}\)
It has its lowest value of \(-1\) at \(90^{\circ}\)
a.why: Sine starts at 0, returns to 0 at \(180^{\circ}\) and ends at 0 at \(360^{\circ}\), so it meets the axis three times. Crossing at \(90^{\circ}\) and \(270^{\circ}\) belongs to cosine, which is the tempting mix-up.
a.clue: Where does sine start, and what is its value there?

b.q: Mia sketches \(y = \cos x\) from \(0^{\circ}\) to \(360^{\circ}\). Where does her graph cross the x-axis?
b.why: Cosine starts at 1, so it is not on the axis at \(0^{\circ}\). It falls to 0 at \(90^{\circ}\) and rises back to 0 at \(270^{\circ}\). The option with three crossings describes sine.
b.clue: Cosine starts at its highest value, not at 0.

a.best: It crosses the x-axis at \(0^{\circ}\), \(180^{\circ}\) and \(360^{\circ}\)
